branches.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment/entry defects, transition-group guard collisions, and wrong local-exit targets by contrasting the NL contracts against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) NL1-INITENTRY-1 requires root->Operate initial entry, but exact source and FCSTM show root's initial edge targets Off, not Operate; Operate is only reached via Off->Operate on 'start', so the exact required initial-entry edge into Operate is absent, and the model reaches Operate only through a non-initial transition rather than a default initial-entry edge from the root scope. (2) All four Operate-substate containment contracts (Idle, AcceleratingOrCruising/'Accelerating or Cruising', Braking) are satisfied by exact parent fields in both source and FCSTM. (3) The Idle->Accelerating and Idle->Cruising group is collapsed in FCSTM: the closed model merges 'Accelerating' and 'Cruising' into one single state 'AcceeleratingOrCruising' rather than two distinct substates/transition alternatives, so NL1-ENDPOINT-IDLE-CRUISE (Idle->Cruising) has no distinct target in the closed model - the group is collapsed into a single edge Idle->AcceleratingOrCruising. Likewise NL1-ENDPOINT-CRUISE-BRAKE (Cruising->Braking) has no distinct Cruising state. (4) NL1-GROUP-1 (Idle->Accelerating as part of the coordinated group) is satisfied via Idle->AcceleratingOrCruising, but the sibling alternative to a distinct Cruising target is missing due to state collapse. (5) NL2 on/off endpoints are satisfied by tr exists Off->Operate/start and Operate->Off (guarded by internal route token, but exact endpoints hold). stage_receipts.reason: NL1 establishes root-level initial entry into Operate and a transition group among Operate's substates (Idle, Accelerating/Cruising, Braking). NL2 establishes the two root-level power transitions triggered by start and keyOff signals. NL3 reinforces that Operate contains substates and that transitions among them are driven by specific actions (accelerating, braking, stopping), which is treated as context reinforcing NL1's group rather than a new endpoint set, since NL3 does not name new distinct substates beyond what NL1 already named. I extracted: (a) initial_entry for root->Operate (from NL1 "system enters the Operate state" after power on), (b) containment contracts for Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking under Operate, (c) transition_groups capturing the substate transitions with Operate as common enclosing owner, (d) endpoint contracts for each transition alternative each carrying exactly one source and one target hint, (e) transition_endpoints for start/keyOff signals with trigger info on transition_groups instead of separate trigger contracts since they are the exact discriminating signal for the alternative (root-off/root-on), (f) state_action is not manufactured since no continuous/repeated activity is explicitly stated, (g) NL3 is covered by an endpoint/group contract capturing the discriminating actions (accelerating, braking, stopping) with proper source/target hints added to the previously incomplete rows NL-CONTRACT-NL1-GROUP-1 (repaired to be a full endpoint contract with source/target) and NL-CONTRACT-NL3-DEPTH-1 (repaired similarly). I did not invent cardinality, guard-disjointness, or state-retention obligations since NL does not explicitly require them.
